title: Placido Domingo at Bradley's
summary: He tells how he met Placido Domingo at Bradley's and joked about doing an opera together.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Chicks, chicks, it's gotta be chicks. I'll bet you that Nastase is a piece of work. I'd like to know him. You know, I met Placido Domingo at Bradley's, of all

The girl that married Bounce, Judy, she used to work up there at Hopper, and he had eyes for her. So she says, 'I'll go out with you if you'll go to Bradley's.' He says, 'Where is Bradley's?' She says, 'I'll show you.' So she took him down to Bradley's and invited me over to the table, and I sat down next to her. Here I am sitting with Placido Domingo. I didn't know who the hell he was. Never heard of him before. And she said, 'BUHBUHBUH-DE-BUHBUHBUH-DE-BUH-DE-BUH-DE-BUH.' You know? I said, 'Sing me somethin'! Right now! Let 'em know you're here. Let out a roar! If you don't, I will.' So he goes into a ...[OPERATIC ROAR]..., big thing, you know -- he just stopped the whole... 'What was that?' Bradley got up and came right over to the table. He says, 'Don't ever do that again.' And then I introduced him. I said, 'This is Placido Domingo. You're not foolin' around with a bum. This is a singer. I mean, this is ace. And he and I are gonna do an opera together. Right, Plack?' By then he had had a couple. He said, 'That's right, Jim.' Bradley went back and sat down, we started talkin' about Carmen. We were gonna do Carmen Lombardo. 'I saw Carmen comin' home from school/He was broke 'cause he was playin' pool...' That
kind of stuff! [LAUGHS] And we were workin' on this thing, you know, and laugh-in.

He gave me some complementary tickets up there, and I heard him sing. Oh boy, he can sing. And I went to his dressing room afterward. He comes out with a bathrobe on, he's wringing wet, and he says, "You see, Jimmy? That's where Jazz comes from!" Heh-heh... "Yes, Placido, I understand." He wouldn't know me now, but he'd remember.

I'll bet he remembered when they first tried to talk about that picture, you know, Carmen, that they advertise in the paper. I'll bet he remembered that night, and started laughing. He probably told everybody about it. He said, "I met this crazy piano player," you know, boom-boom and away we go...
Oh yeah! I don't really have a voice. I just sing with feeling, that's all.
